Appendix C. USINDOPACOM U.S. Indo-Pacific Command’s (USINDOPACOM’s) distinctive geographic and operational characteristics shape the risk drivers outlined in this analysis in ways that differ from other regions, highlighting vulnerabilities surrounding local energy sources (see Section 4.1.3) as well as operational and logistical challenges (see Sections 3.2 and 3.5) that could degrade readiness. In particular, the increasing dependence on China for components of, or investments in, local energy infrastructure (see Sections 4.1.1 and 4.1.2) leave this area vulnerable to local autonomy over energy resources via increasing foreign influence or potential compromise of the energy infrastructure. The primary distinguishing features of this region are the large distances and many islands. Islands face unique energy challenges, including heavy dependence on imported fossil fuels and workforce limitations, especially the shortage of trained technicians required to maintain new advanced energy assets (NLR 2024a).
